questions.topic: Page 11: 1.4 DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO POINTS IN THE 2-D PLANE (Pages 11-13 Focus)
questions.questionText: What is the general formula to calculate the distance between two points $P_{1}(x_{1}, y_{1})$ and $P_{2}(x_{2}, y_{2})$ in a 2-D Cartesian plane?
questions.explanationAnswer: The distance formula derived from the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem is the square root of the sum of the squares of the differences of the x and y coordinates.
questions.explanationQuestion: This question tests the recall of the fundamental distance formula used in 2D coordinate geometry.

questions.topic: Page 11: 1.4 DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO POINTS IN THE 2-D PLANE (Pages 11-13 Focus)
questions.questionText: When a geometric figure like a triangle is reflected across an axis in the Cartesian plane, the lengths of its sides change due to the shift in coordinates.
questions.explanationAnswer: Reflection is an isometry; it preserves the distance between points and thus the lengths of the sides of the figure remain unchanged.
questions.explanationQuestion: This question tests the understanding of geometric properties under reflection as discussed in the text.

questions.topic: Page 11: 1.4 DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO POINTS IN THE 2-D PLANE (Pages 11-13 Focus)
questions.questionText: If a point $P$ has a negative x-coordinate and a positive y-coordinate, in which quadrant does it lie?
questions.explanationAnswer: In the Cartesian plane, Quadrant II is defined by negative x-values and positive y-values.
questions.explanationQuestion: Tests the comprehension of quadrant sign conventions.

questions.topic: Page 11: 1.4 DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO POINTS IN THE 2-D PLANE (Pages 11-13 Focus)
questions.questionText: For any point lying on the x-axis, its ______ coordinate is always zero, and for any point on the y-axis, its ______ coordinate is always zero.
questions.explanationAnswer: The x-axis is defined by y=0, and the y-axis is defined by x=0.

questions.topic: Page 11: 1.4 DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO POINTS IN THE 2-D PLANE (Pages 11-13 Focus)
questions.questionText: Given points $A(1, -8)$, $B(-4, 7)$, and $C(-7, -4)$, show that they are equidistant from the origin $O(0, 0)$. What is the radius of the circle passing through these points?

subjective_evaluation_points.point: Since all distances equal $\sqrt{65}$, the radius is $\sqrt{65}$.

questions.explanationAnswer: All points are at a distance of $\sqrt{65}$ from the origin, satisfying the condition for a circle with radius $\sqrt{65}$.
questions.explanationQuestion: Tests application of distance formula to verify points on a circle.
